title: Minimum Operations to Make Median of Array Equal to K
summary: Given an integer array and a non-negative integer k, determine the least number of operations required to make the median of the array equal to k.
statement: Given an integer array and a non-negative integer k, determine the least number of operations required to make the median of the array equal to k. An operation consists of incrementing or decrementing any array element by one. The median is the middle element in a sorted array; if there are two middle elements, the larger one is chosen.
constraints: nums is a nonempty integer array and k is an integer.
The median is sorted index floor(n/2), so an even-length array uses the larger middle value.
One operation changes one value by one; return the fewest operations making the median exactly k.
hints: After sorting, values on the median’s low side must not exceed k and values on its high side must not fall below k.
Move the median to k, then clamp only violating values on the necessary side.
If median>k, sum value-k for indices through the median where value>k; otherwise sum k-value from the median onward where value<k.
Every counted unit is necessary to keep at least the required number of values on each side of k, and these changes are sufficient.
editorial: Every counted unit is necessary to keep at least the required number of values on each side of k, and these changes are sufficient.

tests.explanation: After sorting, lower the two middle-or-higher values five and five to four, requiring two operations.
The upper median and every value after it must reach at least five, costing three plus one = four.
